item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-23
item.description: One licence text settles this morning. On 2026-11-20 Tencent released the Hy4 flagship — 770B total parameters, 49B active, a one-million-token context — under a document titled the Tencent Hy License, Version 1.0, which opens by saying it is derived from Apache 2.0, is not Apache 2.0, and is not endorsed by the Apache Software Foundation. Section 10 then adds the term that matters: anyone operating a model-as-a-service business with more than USD 50 million of worldwide gross revenue in any twelve-month window, or more than 100 million monthly active users, must obtain a separate written licence from Tencent before using the model or any derivative of it — and the definition of derivative explicitly names fine-tuning, quantisation, distillation, merging and pruning. Hy4 preview, released 28 August, shipped under genuine Apache 2.0 with no use restrictions and is still tagged apache-2.0 on Hugging Face this morning. The same family, the same vendor, two entirely different institutional instruments, four months apart. The repository that carries the new licence was created 2026-10-28, holds five commits, all from one account, and no model weights at all — models live on Hugging Face, ModelScope and GitCode. One more document from the same weekend is the fourth Chinese vendor in this series to attach its own name to a claimed national installation base: 24 million systems, 8,800 ecosystem partners, 160,000 adapted applications. The licence is the day's evidence. The repository is the day's second evidence, and it is quieter.
